caption:
Which skincare actually changes skin, and which only maintains it?
Both sit on the same shelf, and in the jar they look identical.

Maintaining works today and stops working when you stop. Changing works over months, and only counts if it was measured against a control. And a third job - sun protection - prevents, which does the most and gets the least credit.

In a split-face study of 54 middle-aged Japanese women, 26 weeks of a topical retinol produced improvement in fine wrinkles on 50% of treated sides, against 24% of the vehicle sides. One ingredient, one strength, one study. It does not rank products and it does not promise you a result. What it shows is the timescale: months, against a control, on the same face.

So three questions for anything on your shelf. What was it compared to? How long did it take? And what happens if I stop?

Expecting change from a maintainer is how a perfectly good routine gets blamed.

General education only.

first_comment: Most of a routine maintains, and that is the job rather than a failure. Try it tonight: name the job of every bottle on your shelf. Which one surprised you?
